run.question: Show me the logs and resource recommendations for the pod api-gateway in namespace app-102a

report.summary: Logs and configuration for pod api-gateway-585c5579f6-p5xtc in namespace app-102a were retrieved; the workload is running and its container stdout shows a clean nginx start, and the Loki access-log lines returned carry only 2xx INFO entries. No fault, error burst or failure was observed for this pod, so no root cause is named. The resource gap is concrete: the nginx container declares no CPU/memory requests or limits (pod QoS class BestEffort), has no readiness/liveness probes, runs nginx:latest with imagePullPolicy Always, and the Deployment has 1 replica with no HPA. Resource recommendations below are configuration-based advice, not measured-usage sizing, because Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt in this Run.

claims.text: Pod api-gateway-585c5579f6-p5xtc in namespace app-102a exists and is phase Running with its single container nginx Ready, restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason; the pod is owned by ReplicaSet api-gateway-585c5579f6 (controller=true), which is owned by Deployment api-gateway.

The container spec for api-gateway-585c5579f6-p5xtc is: name nginx, image nginx:latest, imagePullPolicy Always, resources {} (no requests, no limits), only containerPort 80/TCP; the pod's QoS class is BestEffort and no readinessProbe or livenessProbe is present in the container spec.

The pod was created 2026-11-21T05:13:08Z (status.startTime identical); kubelet events record Scheduled at 05:13:08.870051Z, then Pulling, Pulled (nginx:latest, 63934605 bytes, 408ms), Created and Started at 05:13:09Z, and Deployment api-gateway recorded ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set api-gateway-585c5579f6 from 0 to 1' at 05:13:08Z. The pod name is younger than the authorized window and was created by its own controller.

Deployment api-gateway in app-102a reports spec.replicas 1 with status readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, and conditions Available (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing (NewReplicaSetAvailable) both True.

The pod's own container logs (container nginx, current instance) contain 23 lines between 2026-11-21T05:13:09.915959Z and 05:13:09.998667Z, all nginx startup output: docker-entrypoint configuration steps, 'Configuration complete; ready for start up', nginx/1.31.9 with 'using the "epoll" event method', OS Linux 6.8.0-149-generic, and start of worker processes 36-43; no error, warning or crash line appears in those 23 lines. The container has no previous instance to read.

A Loki query {namespace="app-102a"} over 2026-11-20T05:13:18Z-2026-11-21T05:13:18Z returned 97 lines from a single stream (namespace=app-102a, pod=api-gateway-585c5579f6-p5xtc, app=nginx, job=nginx, service_name=nginx) with ingest timestamps 2026-11-21T02:33:10Z through 05:13:10Z; every returned line is JSON level INFO, message 'HTTP request completed', with GET paths /health, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/products, /api/v1/inventory, statuses 200, 201 or 204, and response_time_ms between 50 and 198.

The node hosting the pod, opspilot-m1-control-plane, is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False and allocatable cpu 8, memory 32859944Ki, ephemeral-storage 160497381376, pods 110.

Within the 97 Loki access-log lines returned for app-102a, no line carries a 4xx or 5xx status and none is logged above level INFO; this is a newest-first sample of 97 lines covering 02:33:10Z-05:13:10Z, not a complete request or error rate, so it does not prove the absence of errors outside those lines.

The Loki lines are labelled pod=api-gateway-585c5579f6-p5xtc from 2026-11-21T02:33:10Z onward, while the live pod object's creationTimestamp and container startedAt are 2026-11-21T05:13:08Z/05:13:09Z; the two observations conflict and the reason (log backfill, label reuse or another source) could not be determined from the available evidence.

Set explicit CPU and memory requests and limits on the nginx container of Deployment api-gateway (for example requests cpu 100m / memory 128Mi and limits cpu 500m / memory 256Mi as a starting point for an nginx gateway) so the pod leaves the BestEffort QoS class and is not the first to be evicted under node pressure; those numbers should be re-checked against measured container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and container_memory_working_set_bytes once Prometheus is reachable, since no usage data was available in this Run.

Add a readinessProbe and a livenessProbe on container port 80 (HTTP GET /health is already requested by clients per the access logs, so it is a reasonable readiness path) so that endpoint membership and restarts follow actual serving state instead of being assumed from container start.

Replace the nginx:latest tag with a pinned version or digest and, if immutability is desired, set imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent, so a rollout does not silently change the served image; the running image resolves to docker.io/library/import-2026-11-20@sha256:0569bdd230788cb31656ce9d3e47bb84036459391c6931b598c08c9e3494c665 and every pod start currently re-pulls nginx:latest (408ms, 63934605 bytes).

If this gateway must stay available through single-pod disruption, raise spec.replicas above 1 and add a PodDisruptionBudget/topology spread; the Deployment currently runs exactly 1 replica and no HorizontalPodAutoscaler was returned for namespace app-102a by the query that was run.

Consider defining a ResourceQuota and a LimitRange for namespace app-102a so that containers without requests/limits (as this one is) receive defaults; a ResourceQuota query in app-102a returned no rows and LimitRange is not a readable kind in this Run, so the current namespace defaulting is unknown.

Log coverage for the pod is thin: only the current container's 23 startup lines are retained on the node (no previous container instance exists) and the Loki set conflicts with the pod's creationTimestamp (lines labelled with this pod name from 02:33:10Z), so the pod's behaviour before 05:13:08Z is unknown.

Only one pod exists for this workload (single replica), so no cross-pod comparison within app-102a was possible; other pods in otel-demo showed BackOff and Unhealthy events but those belong to different workloads and were not attributed to api-gateway.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so who created or scaled Deployment api-gateway (scaled 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T05:13:08Z) could not be determined.
